item.title: Building a Publishing System That Helps Me Think
item.description:
Over the last few weeks I’ve been writing more.

That has created a slightly unexpected problem.

Writing the article itself was never really the whole problem. I needed somewhere for ideas to start, somewhere they could develop, somewhere finished thinking could live, and a sensible way of sharing it.

For a while those things were all getting mixed together.

I had notes in Obsidian. Drafts developed through conversations. Articles on LinkedIn. Older posts elsewhere. Ideas that were clearly related to one another but were effectively trapped inside individual documents.

item.title: Automating Hugo Site Deployment with GitHub Actions and Private Repositories
item.description:
I’ve always been a proponent of DevOps, and my recent experiments with Hugo have led me to automate the deployment of my site. This post details how I set up an automatic deployment process for my Hugo site using GitHub Actions while keeping my drafts and content private until I’m ready to share them.

Keeping a Private Repository for Hugo Site Definition
#

I have a private repository for my Hugo site definition to keep my draft posts and other content secure until they’re ready for the public. The objective was straightforward: whenever I commit changes to the main branch, Hugo runs, and the result is committed to another repository, specifically my GitHub Pages repo.

item.title: Getting Running With Hugo
item.description:
Choosing the Right Environment for Hugo Development: My Journey to Containers
#

When it comes to setting up a development environment for Hugo, there are numerous options available. My journey in selecting the most suitable one was guided by a desire for efficiency and minimal impact on my primary workstation. Here, I share my experience and rationale behind choosing containers over other methods.

item.title: Getting Started
item.description:
So I’ve started building a new site here as a set of github pages. This has mainly involved playing with couple of site generators, and seeing how I get on with them.

My motivation in this is pretty simple I need to get better at blogging. The tooling I use is a big contributing factor to that. To that end I’ve been trying out a number of platforms and here are the results.
